de5_life.topic: Curtis Yarvin: family, schooling, early career (documented and own account)

claims.text: Yarvin's father was a US foreign service officer; the family was posted to Portugal, Cyprus and the Dominican Republic and earlier lived in Fairfax County, Virginia; his mother, a Protestant from Westchester County, later joined the civil service; parents met at Brown in the mid-1960s; paternal grandparents were Jewish American communists

Yarvin skipped grades, was 11 in ninth grade, a 12-year-old sophomore at a public high school in Columbia, Maryland; at 15 entered Johns Hopkins' Study of Mathematically Precocious Youth and a year later transferred to Brown as a legacy admission; began a CS PhD at Berkeley and left after about a year and a half
Yarvin worked at a mobile software company founded in 1996 as Libris, later Unwired Planet then Phone.com; after the dot-com crash a buyout gave him 'a few hundred thousand dollars'
Yarvin: 'Hoppe opened a kind of door to the pre-revolutionary world for me'

Born 1973 to a liberal, secular family (Tait 2019; Pein 2018); father a diplomat in Nicosia per Yarvin (Raskin interview); Wilde Lake High School 1988 cited to his own 2011 post; Brown 1992; Berkeley CS PhD left after ~1.5 years (Tait; Siegel); sometimes homeschooled by his mother, skipped three grades (Kofman, New Yorker, 2 June 2025)
In the NYT interview (Jan 2025) Yarvin said his parents were career federal civil servants; born 1973 to a diplomat father whose parents were Jewish American communists and a Protestant mother

de5_urbit.topic: Urbit and Tlon: founding, Thiel/Founders Fund money, 2019 exit, 2024-25 return

claims.text: Founders Fund (Thiel) and Andreessen Horowitz invested $1.1 million in Tlon, per Corey Pein, Live Work Work Work Die (2018); first public Urbit code release January 2010 (Yarvin's 13 Jan 2010 post); Yarvin left Tlon in 2019; The Point (Sept 2022) estimated active users at 'a few thousand'
Yarvin returned to a leadership role at Urbit in 2024 as an informal 'wartime C.E.O.'; several top employees resigned in protest (ARTnews 29 Aug 2024; Kofman, New Yorker 2025)
Yarvin, who had left Urbit in January 2019, announced a return 'in a big way' at a public meeting in August 2024; his 2019 departure post was titled 'A Founder's Farewell'

By July 2025 the Urbit Foundation had had four executive directors in about a year; Executive Director Ryan Kneer fired Yarvin from the board, while Yarvin lobbied the other two board members to fire Kneer; Kneer appealed to galaxy holders

July 2025: a newsletter writer who holds Urbit address space reported Yarvin acting as executive director 'by fiat', quoting him calling it 'real Roman times', and reported (terms unknown) a $4M a16z investment for address space earlier in 2025; the Galactic Senate vote outcome was unreported

de5_public.topic: Yarvin's public years: Vance 2021 remark and later engagement

claims.text: Vance on Jack Murphy Live (2021): 'There's this guy, Curtis Yarvin. Who's written about some of these things.' ... 'I'm sympathetic to that project. But another option is that we should just seize the administrative state for our own purposes.'

Vance in a 2021 podcast: 'fire every single mid-level bureaucrat, every civil servant in the administrative state'; 'Replace them with our people'; 'The chief justice has made his ruling. Now let him enforce it.'
The Vance remark dates to September 2021 on a conservative podcast
Yarvin was 'an informal guest of honor' at the 'Coronation Ball', an inaugural gala hosted by Passage Press (Politico's description)
Yarvin: 'I [recently] had lunch with Mike Anton at a coffee shop across the street from the State Department'
Yarvin: 'I've interacted with Vance once since the election. I bumped into him at a party'; Vance greeted him 'Yarvin, you reactionary fascist' (Yarvin's account)
Yarvin on influence: 'how I measure my influence is that I try not to'; the New Right 'is still a vanguard'; people who read him in middle school 'are getting jobs more easily'
Asked if a figure was Peter Thiel, Yarvin: 'No, no, no, this is someone you've never heard of'; Yarvin: 'America just has a really shitty government and needs a new government'
